field remaining_target_positions, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Delete this field. All supplied goals request pressing the button followed by one container pickup. At the pickup decision, the observation includes the requested colored cube before covering and the containers after covering. The annotated field is [] throughout, and it was read at no decision. No incorrect subgoal was reported; the fault is NECESSITY: the target is recoverable from the current observation and goal without carried memory. Replace this field with no memory fields for these single-pickup episodes; there is no value or update event to annotate.

field remaining_target_positions, POLICY PROMPT
  Delete this field for the supplied single-pickup task. The policy observes the uncovered target cube and subsequent covering within the execution shown at the pickup decision, so carrying [] contributes nothing to its choice and violates NECESSITY. Remove the instruction to write [] and all initialization, retention, and removal instructions for this field. No memory update is needed: choose using the goal and the currently supplied observation. This deletion is supported by the supplied single-pickup episodes, not by evidence that ordered target memory is unnecessary for multiple-pickup tasks.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  The supplied goals each request a button press and one container pickup. Their pickup observations include both the pre-covering colored cubes and the resulting resting containers; the unused memory is [] throughout. No subgoal failure was reported, so preserve the existing single-pickup behavior while removing dependencies on the deleted field and the multiple-pickup branches from this task's policy prompt. In the initial scene, with uncovered cubes and no completed press in the observed execution, choose A. When the observed execution shows button contact followed by withdrawal, choose B; explicit pressed-down text is not required. Locate the goal's requested cube color in the pre-covering frames of this same observation, then follow its covering event to the corresponding resting container. If only before-and-after covering frames are available, select the resting container nearest that cube position. Point inside its current visible body rather than at the button or another container; small center offsets are expected. A successful lift completes the single-pickup task, without an additional put-down. Remove list-based continuation, release, and fallback rules here: they serve multiple-pickup goals absent from this minibatch and cannot reference a deleted field.
